extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, policy makers, researchers and practitioners using WIPO plant variety and GI statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, counting rules and data‑quality notes used in WIPO's 2019 plant variety and geographical indication (GI) statistics. Covers equivalent vs absolute counts, origin determination, GI definitions and reporting categories/limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent count (treatment of regional offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent counts take multiple members of the regional office into account. For the equivalent count, a single application filed at a regional office is equivalent to multiple applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To calculate the number of equivalent applications at a regional office in 2019, each application has been multiplied by the corresponding number of member states for the regional office concerned. For CPVO applications, if the applicant resided in one of the 28 EU member states, the application was counted as one resident filing and 27 filings abroad. If the applicant did not reside in an EU member state, the application was counted as 28 filings abroad. The same methodology was applied to OAPI member states. Equivalent counts therefore raise the ranking of countries whose applicants file intensively at regional offices (e.g., Netherlands moves up when equivalent counts are applied). See map 4.5 and note in D9–D11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute count (regional office treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: For absolute counts, an application received by a regional office is counted only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute counts do not expand regional filings into multiple equivalent filings. Data tables that state 'based on absolute count, not equivalent count' should be interpreted accordingly (e.g., D10, D12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of application/title (determined by applicant residence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of an application (or of titles issued) is determined by the residence of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications by origin include resident applications and applications filed abroad. 'Regional' refers to applications filed at regional offices (e.g., CPVO). This rule underpins the breakdowns of resident/abroad/regional in D10–D13 and the equivalent‑absolute translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not compare applications and titles for the same year
rubrics_metrics.description: Data on applications for a given year should not be compared with data on titles issued for the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure for issuing titles varies across offices and there are differences in the time lag between application and title issue dates. Fluctuations in titles granted may reflect processing capacity or procedural delays rather than application activity in the same year (see note in D8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident and non‑resident classification and contribution to growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics separate resident and non‑resident (abroad) filings and report resident share (%) and non‑resident share, as well as the contribution of each to total growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and charts (e.g., D3, D5, D6) show resident share and non‑resident share and decompose total growth into contributions from resident and non‑resident filings. Example: 'applications in Poland grew by 23.3%, and resident applications contributed 7.8 percentage points to this total growth, while non‑resident applications accounted for the other 15.5 percentage points.'

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO data coverage and estimation (partial reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals and many aggregates are WIPO estimates based on partial reporting (e.g., 'World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 70 offices').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different figures use different coverage (e.g., world totals from 70 offices; GI data from 117 national/regional authorities; product category distribution based on 80 jurisdictions). Data are partial/incomplete and should be interpreted with caution. Footnotes indicate offices that did not report data or used earlier years for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Geographical Indication (GI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication (GI) is a sign identifying a good as originating from a specific geographical area and possessing a given quality, reputation or other characteristic that is essentially attributable to that geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main function of a GI is to indicate a connection between the quality, reputation or other characteristics of a good and its territory of origin. GIs can be protected through various legal means (sui generis, trademarks, regional systems, international agreements, other national legal means).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting GIs to minimize double counting
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize double counting, GIs in force through the European Union regional system, the African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI) and the Lisbon System are counted once only rather than multiplied by the number of member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite this, the total still may include some double counting because GIs in force through bilateral, plurilateral or multilateral agreements could be included multiple times. Notes and footnotes explain which systems/data are included for each jurisdiction (see figures 5.1–5.3 and table 5.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal means categories for reporting GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs are reported broken down by legal means of protection: sui generis systems, trademark laws, regional systems, international agreements, and other national legal means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questionnaire asked for GIs protected through these categories. Many countries did not provide statistics on GIs protected through trademark systems—this may reflect either non‑use of trademarks for GIs or difficulty identifying GIs among collective and certification trademarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product category classification for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs in force are classified by product category (wines and spirits; agricultural products and foodstuffs; handicrafts; services; others/unknown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution (2019): wines and spirits 56.6%, agricultural products and foodstuffs 34.2%, handicrafts 3.5%, services 0.1%, others/unknown 5.6%. Some jurisdictions did not provide breakdowns by product category so the distribution uses data from a subset (e.g., 80 jurisdictions); Czech Republic, France and Italy product‑category data and Lisbon System data may be missing from this breakdown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent/absolute count ratio for abroad filing analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The equivalent/absolute count ratio is used to show how much regional filings inflate abroad equivalents and to compare absolute vs equivalent counts for filings and titles abroad (e.g., charts in D11 and D13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ratio highlights origins that file intensively via regional offices (high equivalent/absolute ratios). Figures list absolute and equivalent counts side‑by‑side to illustrate the effect (e.g., Netherlands, Germany, France show high equivalent counts when CPVO filings are expanded). See D11/D13 notes.
